newsitem.title: USA: United to start pacific freighters in March.
newsitem.headline: United to start pacific freighters in March.

text.p: United Airlines said Thursday it is moving ahead with its plan to launch a transpacific freighter service in March, starting with a pair of DC-10-30 aircraft.

A spokesman said no launch date or schedule would be made public until March 3. The airline said in a statement the initial points served will be Chicago, Los Angeles and Anchorage on the US side, and Osaka, Manila and Taipei on the Asian side.
Two more DC-10-30 freighters will join the service in September for the pre-Christmas peak. At that point, service will be extended to New York, San Francisco and Tokyo.

The startup of the freighter service, which will complement United's bellyhold cargo operations on passenger flights, was originally set for September 1996, then deferred to March by the airline, citing a lack of availability of the right aircraft.
At the time, market sources also blamed concern about overcapacity at the start of the year for the delay, but the year has started strongly for the US-Asia air freight market.
Earlier UAL announced record 1996 cargo revenue saying it was based on an 8.3 percent increase in mail revenues and a 2.4 rise in freight revenues.

Strong gains were recorded on the North Atlantic, with cargo revenues up 21.1 percent and tonne miles up 15.8 percent, mainly due to the increased capacity and improved freight utilization provided by the airline's growing fleet of Boeing 777 twinjets. - Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom Tel +44 171 542 7706 Fax +5017
